status: canonical historical genealogy + timeline/map projection contract
purpose: Represent major religious traditions as dated, branching historical lineages. Nodes can be trunks, schisms, reforms, schools, mystical currents or institutional crystallizations. The structure is designed for timeline, spiral and map projection without pretending every tradition has one exact birthday.
epistemic_rule: Traditional/sacred origin claims, historical reconstruction, institutional dates and project visualization coordinates remain distinct. A genealogy edge describes historical relation, not theological truth, superiority, legitimacy or identity.

date_policy.exact_date: Use only for well-attested formal events such as a charter, council, declaration or organizational meeting.
date_policy.marker_year: A conventional or high-information branch marker inside a longer process; never silently treated as the whole origin.
date_policy.formation_window: Preferred for gradual crystallization, diffuse movements and retrospective denominational identities.
date_policy.deep_origin: Use broad ranges where evidence does not justify a narrow date.
date_policy.bce_encoding: Negative astronomical-style integers are used only for sorting/projection; display labels retain BCE/CE notation and do not introduce a historical year zero.

node_types.trunk: Large lineage/family with substantial historical continuity.
node_types.phase: Major historical state of a lineage before or after a transformation.
node_types.communion: Family of churches sharing communion or doctrinal/institutional identity.
node_types.denomination: Differentiated institutional tradition within a larger family.
node_types.school: Legal, philosophical or interpretive school; not automatically a separate religion.
node_types.reform_movement: Movement seeking change inside or from an inherited tradition.
node_types.schism_lineage: Lineage differentiated by a rupture or contested succession.
node_types.mystical_current: Cross-cutting current that may exist in several branches.
node_types.monastic_lineage: Transmission lineage centered on monastic institutions/practice.
node_types.sister_lineage: Related lineage with shared ancestry but not safely represented as a child.

edge_types.differentiates_from: Identity becomes distinguishable over time without one clean break.
edge_types.splits_from: A rupture produces durable differentiated communities.
edge_types.reforms_within: Movement begins as reform of an inherited tradition.
edge_types.institutionalizes_from: A diffuse current becomes a durable institution or denomination.
edge_types.legal_school_within: Juristic school inside a broader religious family.
edge_types.mystical_current_within: Mystical/devotional current crossing ordinary institutional branches.
edge_types.communion_member: Ancient/local church participating in a later communion; not implied to have been founded when the communion divided.
edge_types.predecessor_to: Immediate historical predecessor whose identity is not simply retained.

spiral_projection_contract.thesis: Foundation nodes unfold outward from historical time. They are not dimensions and radial distance never represents spiritual height, truth, value, age-prestige or authority.
spiral_projection_contract.radial_variable: seed_year or formation-window midpoint in a selected historical epoch transform
spiral_projection_contract.angular_variable: layout only: family and sibling separation; angle has no doctrinal ranking
spiral_projection_contract.branch_curve: child trajectory begins at its parent/ancestor branch marker and receives its own later radial trajectory
spiral_projection_contract.multi_parent_rule: Syncretic or mixed-origin nodes may connect to more than one predecessor; do not force a false single-parent tree.
spiral_projection_contract.uncertainty_render: Wide/uncertain dates render as arcs or fuzzy bands rather than exact points.
spiral_projection_contract.event_vs_foundation: Councils, destructions, migrations and succession crises may be branch events without being independent religious foundations.
spiral_projection_contract.map_link: Every node may carry an origin_place or distributed_origin for geographic projection. Present-day demographic geography remains a separate dated layer.

families.name: Israelite / Jewish lineages

nodes.name: Israelite/Judahite religious formation
nodes.notes: Deep substrate rather than a single founded religion.

nodes.name: Post-exilic / Persian-period Judaism
nodes.notes: Torah/scriptural authority and portable communal forms become increasingly central.

nodes.name: Second Temple Jewish field

seed_clock.date_or_range: Second Temple period, c. 516 BCE–70 CE

nodes.notes: A plural religious field, not one denomination.

nodes.name: Rabbinic Judaism
nodes.notes: Do not model Pharisees as a proven one-step parent. Mishnah c. 200; rabbinization is gradual and much later.

nodes.name: Karaite Judaism
nodes.notes: Scripture-centered non-rabbinic Jewish movement; Anan ben David is important but sole-founder narratives should remain qualified.

nodes.name: Medieval Kabbalistic currents

origin.place: southern France / Iberia and wider Jewish networks

nodes.notes: Cross-cutting mystical traditions, not a denomination.

nodes.name: Hasidic Judaism

origin.place: Podolia and eastern European Jewish communities

nodes.notes: Baal Shem Tov-associated revival; later diversified into dynastic/group lineages.

nodes.name: Reform / Liberal Judaism
nodes.notes: Modern movement has earlier precursors; Hamburg gives a strong institutional seed marker, not the sole intellectual origin.

nodes.name: Orthodox Judaism as modern denominational identity
nodes.notes: Traditional halakhic practice is far older; 'Orthodox' becomes a modern denominational identity partly through response to Reform/modernity.

nodes.name: Conservative / Masorti Judaism
nodes.notes: JTS was founded in 1886 and became a central institutional engine; intellectual precursors include nineteenth-century Positive-Historical Judaism.

nodes.name: Samaritan Israelite tradition
nodes.notes: Do not render Samaritanism as a denomination born from rabbinic Judaism.

integrity: Judaism has multiple valid clocks; no single seed year represents the whole tradition.
Second Temple sects, rabbinic Judaism, Karaism, medieval mysticism and modern denominations must stay historically distinct.
Modern Orthodox/Reform/Conservative labels must not be projected unchanged into antiquity.

families.name: Christian lineages

nodes.name: Early Christianity / Jesus movement
nodes.notes: Historically emerges within the Second Temple Jewish world and rapidly becomes translocal.

nodes.name: Nicene Christian consolidation

origin.place: Nicaea / Constantinople and Roman imperial church networks

nodes.notes: Council markers are doctrinal consolidation events, not the birth of all churches receiving them.

nodes.name: Church of the East lineage
nodes.notes: Ancient Mesopotamian Christianity predates 431; the council is a differentiation marker, not an origin from nothing.

nodes.name: Chalcedonian Christian family
nodes.notes: Receives the Chalcedonian definition.

nodes.name: Oriental Orthodox / non-Chalcedonian communion family

origin.place: Egypt, Syria, Armenia and connected regions

nodes.notes: Constituent churches have pre-451 roots; 451 marks enduring non-reception of Chalcedon, not their creation ex nihilo.

nodes.name: Latin Western Christian tradition
nodes.notes: Gradual linguistic, political, canonical and ecclesiological differentiation.

nodes.name: Greek/Eastern Chalcedonian tradition
nodes.notes: Gradual differentiation; includes multiple patriarchates/churches, not one ethnicity.

nodes.name: Roman Catholic Church, post-schism Western trajectory
nodes.notes: Do not present 1054 as the date the Roman Church itself first existed.

nodes.name: Eastern Orthodox communion, post-schism trajectory
nodes.notes: 1054 is a conventional marker in a centuries-long separation; 1204 further hardened it.

nodes.name: Protestant Reformation family

origin.place: Wittenberg and multiple European reform centers

nodes.notes: Not one denomination; multiple Reformation streams emerged independently/interactively.

nodes.name: Lutheran tradition
nodes.notes: 1530 is a strong confessional consolidation marker.

nodes.name: Reformed tradition
nodes.notes: Zwinglian and Calvinian trajectories should not be flattened into one founder/date.

nodes.name: Church of England / Anglican trajectory
nodes.notes: Has both institutional continuity with medieval English Christianity and Reformation-era doctrinal/liturgical transformation.

nodes.name: Anabaptist traditions

seed_clock.date_or_range: 21 Jan 1525 Zürich baptisms; 1527 Schleitheim consolidation marker

nodes.notes: Multiple Radical Reformation streams; Zürich Brethren are a high-information institutional seed.

nodes.name: Methodist traditions
nodes.notes: Begins as an Anglican revival movement; later Methodist denominations institutionalize separately.

nodes.name: Adventist traditions
nodes.notes: Adventism is broader than Seventh-day Adventism; 1863 is the SDA organizational date.

nodes.name: Pentecostal movement
nodes.notes: Heavily shaped by Holiness currents; later becomes globally diverse and cross-denominational.

nodes.name: Evangelical movement/current
nodes.notes: Cross-denominational movement rather than a single church; later evangelical identities diversify substantially.

integrity: Council dates are doctrinal/institutional markers, not magical creation dates.
Oriental Orthodox and Church of the East churches have roots older than the councils associated with later differentiation.
1054 must render as a symbolic branch marker inside a longer East-West process, with 1204 as another major hardening event.
Protestantism is a family of reform trajectories, not one church.
Evangelicalism, Pentecostalism and some renewal movements may cross denominational boundaries.

families.name: Islamic lineages

nodes.name: Early Islam / Qur'anic community
nodes.notes: 622 Hijra is a particularly strong community/institutional clock inside this formation.

nodes.name: Sunni Islam, formative majority tradition

origin.place: Medina, Damascus, Baghdad and wider caliphal networks

nodes.notes: Do not represent Sunni Islam as fully formed on the day of Muhammad's death; later hadith, law and theology crystallize over centuries.

nodes.name: Shiʿi / Alid-imamate traditions

seed_clock.date_or_range: 632 succession dispute; 680 Karbala as major formative marker

origin.place: Medina / Kufa / Karbala and wider networks

nodes.notes: Shiʿi identity and doctrine develop through several succession crises and imamate lineages.

nodes.name: Kharijite / Muhakkima early current
nodes.notes: Early third trajectory distinct from both later Sunni and Shiʿi authority structures.

nodes.name: Ibadi Islam
nodes.notes: Historical scholarship relates Ibadism to early Muhakkima/Kharijite fields; Ibadis developed distinct self-understanding and jurisprudence, so avoid using 'Kharijite' as a simplistic present-day label.

nodes.name: Hanafi legal school

origin.place: Kufa / Baghdad and wider eastern networks

nodes.notes: Named for Abu Hanifa (d. 767); school formation continues through students and later jurists.

nodes.name: Maliki legal school
nodes.notes: Named for Malik b. Anas (d. 795); regional institutionalization continues later.

nodes.name: Shafiʿi legal school
nodes.notes: Named for al-Shafiʿi (d. 820); later jurists consolidate the school.

nodes.name: Hanbali legal school
nodes.notes: Named for Ahmad ibn Hanbal (d. 855); later jurists institutionalize the madhhab.

nodes.name: Zaydi Shiʿism

seed_clock.date_or_range: 740 CE revolt of Zayd and subsequent lineage formation

nodes.notes: Use 740 as a major marker, not a claim that all Zaydi doctrine/institutions appeared instantly.

nodes.name: Ismaili Shiʿism

seed_clock.date_or_range: post-765 succession differentiation; organized daʿwa by 9th century

nodes.notes: Linked to succession after Jaʿfar al-Sadiq (d. 765); later Fatimid and missionary institutions transform the movement.

nodes.name: Twelver / Imami Shiʿism

origin.place: Samarra / Baghdad and wider Imami networks

nodes.notes: Occultation crisis strongly shapes Twelver theological/institutional crystallization; earlier Imami lineage predates 874.

nodes.name: Nizari Ismaili lineage
nodes.notes: Emerges from the 1094 Nizar/Mustaʿli succession split.

nodes.name: Mustaʿli Ismaili lineage

origin.place: Cairo → Yemen / western India in later developments

nodes.notes: Later Tayyibi and other developments require their own children.

nodes.name: Sufi / tasawwuf currents
nodes.notes: Cross-cuts Sunni and Shiʿi histories; later tariqas/orders should be modeled as descendant institutional lineages, not as a third Sunni/Shia denomination.

integrity: 632 is a succession rupture, not a complete one-day birth of Sunni and Shia identities.
Legal madhhabs are schools within Sunni Islam, not separate religions.
Ibadism needs its own historical/self-identity treatment rather than being flattened into a generic modern Kharijite label.
Sufism is a cross-cutting mystical current with later orders, not a single denomination.
Twelver 874/941 and Ismaili 765/1094 dates are crystallization/succession markers inside older Shiʿi histories.

families.name: Buddhist lineages

nodes.name: Early Buddhist sangha
nodes.notes: Historical Buddha chronology is debated; avoid one exact birthday.

nodes.name: Sri Lankan Theravada-associated monastic lineage

seed_clock.date_or_range: 3rd century BCE transmission to Sri Lanka

nodes.notes: Theravada as a modern umbrella should not be projected unchanged onto all ancient communities.

nodes.name: Mahayana movements

seed_clock.date_or_range: c. 1st century BCE–2nd century CE emergence

nodes.notes: Early Mahayana likely involved loose currents within existing monasteries, not an immediate separate church.

nodes.name: Vajrayana / tantric Buddhist traditions

origin.place: South Asia → Tibet/Himalaya and wider Asia

nodes.notes: Multiple tantric textual and practice lineages; no single founder.

integrity: Do not force early Buddhist schools into a simple surviving-denomination tree.
Mahayana and Vajrayana are broad movement families with overlapping institutions and texts.

families.name: Hindu/Vedic-derived traditions

nodes.name: Vedic religious field
nodes.notes: Deep substrate; not identical to later Hinduism.

nodes.name: Hindu traditions / long formation

seed_clock.date_or_range: late Vedic, epic, Puranic and devotional formation, broad window

nodes.notes: No single founder or seed date; 'Hinduism' is a later umbrella for many interacting traditions.

nodes.name: Vaishnava traditions

seed_clock.date_or_range: late centuries BCE–early centuries CE crystallization

nodes.notes: Includes multiple Vishnu/Krishna/Rama devotional and theological lineages.

nodes.name: Shaiva traditions

seed_clock.date_or_range: late centuries BCE–early centuries CE crystallization

nodes.notes: Vedic Rudra background and multiple later Shaiva sectarian/philosophical systems.

nodes.name: Shakta traditions

seed_clock.date_or_range: c. 4th–7th centuries CE major textual/sectarian crystallization

nodes.notes: Goddess worship is older than this window; this marks stronger sectarian/textual crystallization, not first goddess devotion.

integrity: Vaishnava, Shaiva and Shakta traditions are internally plural and overlap regionally and philosophically.

families.name: Jain lineages

nodes.name: Jain / Jina tradition, Mahavira-associated historical formation
nodes.notes: Jain tradition remembers earlier Tirthankaras; historical reconstruction should preserve that sacred chronology separately.

nodes.name: Śvetāmbara Jain tradition

seed_clock.date_or_range: early centuries CE → late-5th-century textual stabilization

nodes.notes: The split with Digambara is not securely reducible to one exact year.

nodes.name: Digambara Jain tradition
nodes.notes: Later sectarian narratives of one dramatic split are historically difficult; use gradual differentiation.

integrity: Do not use a single traditional schism year as settled history; scholarship emphasizes gradual differentiation.

families.name: Other major foundation anchors — first pass

nodes.name: Sikh tradition
nodes.notes: Community and institutions develop through successive Gurus.

nodes.name: Khalsa
nodes.notes: A major refoundation/disciplinary community marker within Sikh history.

nodes.name: Bábí movement
nodes.notes: Immediate predecessor field of the Baháʼí Faith.

nodes.name: Baháʼí Faith
nodes.notes: Baháʼí identity increasingly replaces Bábí after the 1863 declaration.

nodes.name: Zoroastrian tradition / Zarathustra-associated reform

seed_clock.date_or_range: plausible scholarly range c. 13th–6th century BCE; many favor around 1000 BCE

origin.place: eastern Iranian / Central Asian region, uncertain

nodes.notes: Must render as a wide uncertainty band; exact date and place remain debated.

integrity: This section is intentionally incomplete; future waves should deepen Sikh sub-lineages, Baháʼí administrative clocks, Chinese traditions, Shinto, Yoruba/Ifa and indigenous traditions without forcing them into Abrahamic branching logic.

cross_family_connections.note: Christianity historically emerges from the Second Temple Jewish environment while becoming a distinct tradition.
Christian communities/textual traditions formed part of the late antique environment encountered by early Islam; this is context, not a parent-child edge.
Jewish communities/traditions formed part of Arabia and the broader late-antique Near Eastern context; do not render Islam as simply a branch of Judaism.
The Bábí movement arose within a Twelver Shiʿi Persian context but became a distinct new religious movement.

future_research_queue: Christianity: deepen Baptist, Presbyterian, Congregational, Quaker, Restorationist/Latter-day Saint, African-initiated, independent and Oriental Orthodox constituent church histories.
Islam: deepen Sufi tariqas, Tayyibi/Daudi Bohra lineages, Ahmadiyya, Salafi reform currents, regional institutions and theological schools without treating all as equivalent node types.
Judaism: add Reconstructionist, Renewal, Haredi/Modern Orthodox, Sephardi/Mizrahi institutional histories and Kabbalistic schools with carefully dated formation windows.
Buddhism: add early schools, Chan/Zen, Pure Land, Tibetan schools and modern reform lineages.
Hindu traditions: expand sampradayas, Vedanta schools, bhakti movements, Tantra and regional temple lineages without inventing one universal branch tree.
Map indigenous and diasporic traditions using distributed-origin polygons/routes where a point seed would be misleading.
Attach canonical texts, councils, teachers, institutions and sacred places as separate typed nodes rather than stuffing them into tradition identity.
Add branch-by-branch geography through dated diffusion events, not current-country coloring projected backward in time.
